description: Restructure the designs so every part is independently versioned (Arm, Mount, Base, Gripper, Handle, Aero Hand) and published separately. The live preview has one version dropdown per part and assembles the current selection, with shared interfaces between parts so any version of one fits any version of its neighbor where possible, and it flags incompatible combos. Per-part scheme is in AGENTS.md (Arm 1 = reBot B601-RS import, Mount 1 = reBot wrist mount from Base 10, Aero Hand 1). Related: voice-bbe0e945 (mix-and-match picker), voice-bed52066 (rename), voice-3cd78d20 (reBot arm mount), voice-c0e340c7 (Aero Hand assembly).

results.identified_issue: Rule lives in Scripts/publish_designs.py discover(): rows whose carries include 'Aero Hand' get name 'Aero Hand N assembly' (so gallery partVersion() no longer matches them as a Base); carried-part claiming now sorts by folder name, not version, so renaming doesn't change which folder owns Arm 1/Mount 1 (still v310). on_mount comes from param_value(folder,'aero_view_x'); Mount 1's own Aero plate (from v310) is shifted by the Aero Hand's on_mount, which assumes v310 and v313 share aero_view_x/tool_z (verified via STL bounds: both hub z -98..-92, aero_plate x 201.6..258.4). gallery.js buildMix(): aeroOnHub = aero && !base nulls gripper/handles and adds model.shift; applyExplosion adds mesh.userData.shift. If a future Mount/Aero version changes aero_view_x independently, put on_mount on the Mount too. Aero+Base together is not flagged (one tool at a time on the hub, hand shown on the rack).
results.summary: Aero Hand is now its own end effector: Arm 1 + Mount 1 + Aero Hand 1 assembles on the Mount with no Base and no warning, and Base 13 is gone from the Base picker
results.detailed_description:
Base 13 no longer appears as a Base option. The publisher now treats any folder whose VERSIONS.txt heading carries an Aero Hand (v313) as that hand's assembly and names it "Aero Hand 1 assembly". It keeps its own tile, its Tune panel and its saved link, but it isn't offered in the Base picker anymore, so the newest Base is now Base 12. I didn't renumber or rename any folders.

To put the Aero Hand on the arm, set Base to "No base" and Aero Hand to 1. The Gripper and Handle pickers then read "Aero Hand instead", and the hand moves off the rack beside the arm onto Mount 1's hub, in the spot where the gripper's tool plate would go. The Mount shows only the plate for the tool you've picked: the Aero plate with the hand, the gripper plate otherwise. The warning bar shows nothing for Arm 1 + Mount 1 + Aero Hand 1. The link for that view is ?base=none&arm=1&mount=1&aero=1. If you pick a Base and the Aero Hand together, the hand stays on the rack beside the arm, the way Base 13 used to show it.

How it's done: the hand was exported 230 mm to the side (aero_view_x in v313's params.json). The publisher reads that number and stores it on Aero Hand 1 as on_mount = [-230, 0, 0], and the preview moves the hand and its plate back by that much. Before relying on that, I checked that v310 and v313 export the hub and both tool plates at exactly the same coordinates.

Checks: I took a headless Chrome screenshot of Arm 1 + Mount 1 + Aero Hand 1 (attached). The publisher tests pass, including a new one for the assembly rename and on_mount. test_gripper_poses still fails only on the old Base 6 (v306), as it did before. In AGENTS.md I changed only the Aero Hand 1 row of the per-part table.

results.notes: Steer from Jake (via coordinator): in the per-part picker, Aero Hand is its own end-effector part, not a Base version. Base 13 (voice-c0e340c7) should not appear as a Base option; treat it as Aero Hand 1's assembly. Aero Hand must be selectable as the Arm's end effector directly on the Mount (Mount 1, reBot wrist mount), as an alternative to Base+Gripper, and the incompatibility bar should accept Arm 1 + Mount 1 + Aero Hand 1 with no Base. A separate pebble covers the top-level design-family dropdown and the AGENTS.md family rewrite, so keep AGENTS.md edits to the per-part table.

results.identified_issue: Carried parts are split out in Scripts/publish_designs.py discover() using the CARRIED name regexes and VERSIONS.txt heading tokens. Derived rows reuse the carrier's folder and source but skip params (no Tune). Lineage comes from lineage(): a heuristic on free-text VERSIONS entries, so odd phrasing gives odd gists (Handle 4: 'with every dimension a named'). If Jake wants exact taglines, add an explicit field to the headings. gallery.js mixFlags() holds the compatibility rules, and CARRIED in gallery.js must match the publisher's regexes. v310's palm-only 'Aero Hand (left)' reference isn't claimed by any Aero Hand version, so it is hidden from Base 10's option and shows only on Base 10's own tile.
results.summary: The live preview now has six part pickers (Gripper, Handle, Base, Arm, Mount, Aero Hand), each version says what it builds on, and bad combinations get a warning
results.detailed_description:
Arm 1, Mount 1 and Aero Hand 1 are now published as their own designs, so they get their own tiles and their own pickers in the mix-and-match tile. Base 10's heading in VERSIONS.txt now ends with ', Arm 1, Mount 1' and Base 13's with ', Arm 1, Mount 1, Aero Hand 1'. The publisher reads that and takes those parts out of the Base by name (reBot Arm…, Wrist hub / Tool plate / Aero Hand tool plate, Aero Hand (left)…). That means choosing a Base no longer pulls in the arm or the hand. Arm, Mount and Aero Hand start out turned off so the tile still opens on the gripper; ?arm=1&mount=1&aero=1 turns them on.

Lineage, as you asked: each option shows what it builds on, read from VERSIONS.txt rather than typed in by hand. You'll see 'Base 12 (from Base 11, on the STS3215 only)' and 'Base 13 (from Base 11, on the RobStride RS00 with the whole left Aero…)', which makes clear 13 comes from 11 and not from 12. The rule is the first other '<Kind> N' after the colon in each entry, skipping anything in parentheses, plus the words up to the next stop. Entries that don't name a parent (Base 1, Base 3, Gripper 13) show just the bare name. No versions were renumbered.

Interface warnings show in an amber bar in the tile. They come from catalog data, not part names: fingers that aren't the ones a Handle or Base was built on; a Base that doesn't fit the chosen Mount (hand-held Bases such as 12 have no wrist bracket); a Base or Aero Hand on an Arm with no Mount; and a Mount or Aero Hand built for a different Arm or Mount version. I checked it in headless Chrome: Arm 1 + Mount 1 + Base 13 + Aero Hand 1 assembles with no warning, and Base 12 on Mount 1 shows the bracket warning (screenshot).

Tests: publisher tests pass, including a new one. test_gripper_poses now skips Arm, Mount and Aero Hand, which have no jaws. It still fails on Base 6 (v306, kept unfinished with no poses.js entry); that failure was there before this change. Known limits: Handle↔Base has no check because every Handle is meant to fit every Base. A Handle picked while a Base with handle-gears is chosen still shows 'Handle in Base'. When the warning bar is showing it covers the tile's name label.

summary: The live preview's per-part picker wrongly lists Base 13 as a Base option, and Aero Hand cannot be chosen directly as the Arm's end effector on Mount 1. Aero Hand should be its own part (Base 13 becomes its assembly), selectable instead of Base+Gripper, with Arm 1 + Mount 1 + Aero Hand 1 passing the compatibility check.
